definition: Used as the object of a verb or preposition in formal English.
exampleSentence: Dr. Aris, with whom we conducted the field trials, received an international award.

definition: Belonging to or associated with which person.
exampleSentence: The institute, whose research focuses on clean energy, secured major government backing.

definition: Used referring to something previously mentioned in non-defining clauses.
exampleSentence: The cathedral, which was completed in 1380, dominates the city skyline.

definition: Accompanying but not forming an essential part of something.
exampleSentence: Non-defining relative clauses provide incidental information rather than essential identification.
The conference center, which was built last year, features noteworthy acoustic design.
Non-defining clauses supply supplementary biographical details regarding the author.

definition: Tending to elaborate or add decorative detail.
exampleSentence: The editor excised elaborative parenthetical clauses to sharpen the expository prose.

definition: Pointing indirectly toward someone's guilt; incidental.
exampleSentence: Such circumstantial descriptors, set off by commas, provide vivid narrative texture.

definition: A remark that is not directly related to the main topic of discussion.
exampleSentence: The author inserted an ironic parenthetical aside, which delighted astute readers.

definition: A temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.
exampleSentence: His essay contains an entertaining digression, which explores Renaissance alchemy.
